hints.title: Triplet Proximity Search Obstacle
hints.text: Testing all triplets requires cubic time. If you sort the collection and fix the first number, how can you adjust the remaining two elements toward the target sum without checking every combination?

hints.title: Monotonic Triplet Squeeze
hints.text: After sorting, fixing the first element allows two pointers to scan inward. If the current sum is less than target, increase the sum by advancing the left marker; if greater, decrease by moving the right marker.

hints.title: Sorted Triplet Traversal Procedure
hints.text: Sort the array. Initialize closest to the sum of the first three numbers. For each index i from zero to n minus three, skip duplicate values of nums[i]. Set left to i plus one and right to n minus one. While left is less than right, calculate sum. If sum equals target, return immediately. Update closest if the absolute difference is smaller. Move left or right depending on whether sum is below or above target.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (3 <= N <= 500)
complexity.notes: O(N^2) sorted two-pointer sweep with O(1) auxiliary space beyond sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all C(N, 3) triplets takes O(N^3) time, which is too slow for N=500 (~2 * 10^7 operations).
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting in O(N log N) enables reducing the two inner loops to an O(N) inward pointer scan.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Early return when curr == target, skipping duplicate outer elements, and avoiding 32-bit integer overflow.
